label: r2c3
name: flipped trunk, 128 updates
hypothesis: Uses the flipped-trunk network with n_envs 64 and 8 minibatches of 128 samples. That gives about 128 updates, against 64 in r1c3. In round 1, going from 32 to 64 updates raised dev success from 0.70 to 0.90, so halving the batch again may speed learning further. Refuted if it scores clearly below the flipped trunk at 64 updates (the other proposal), which would mean the batches are now too small and too noisy.
last_analysis: Lining the features up with the mirrored landing columns was the decisive change. Without it the starting network scored 0. A fixed flip scored 0.70 to 0.93, and a learned column remap reached only 0.10. After that, the recipe mattered most. Going from 32 to 64 updates raised success from 0.70 to 0.90. r2c3 (flipped trunk, 64 worlds, 4 epochs, about 128 updates) is best at 0.928. r2c1 (2 epochs, 128 worlds) and r2c2 (flipped trunk, 64 updates) both scored about 0.92, the same within noise. In round 3, every run that used 2 epochs with 64 worlds (about 236 small updates) collapsed to DONE on both seeds, or nearly so. That includes the deeper-trunk and global-context runs, so those two ideas were never properly tested. Their recipe was the confound. Safe recipes so far use at least about 2k samples per update or 4 epochs. Remaining errors are probably wrong ordering under overhangs or stopping at the wrong time (IoU 0.989 against 0.92 success).
